Technical Report: Mars Mission Training Simulation & Web Migration

1. Executive Summary

The Mars Mission Training Simulation is an interactive, multi-stage educational game designed to train future astronauts through a comprehensive 5-day Martian mission workflow. Originally developed in Python, the project blends programming logic with real-world space engineering, planetary geology, and orbital mechanics based on official NASA scientific data. To enhance accessibility and user experience for the final presentation, the application was successfully migrated into an interactive web interface using HTML and JavaScript with the assistance of ChatGPT.

2. Game Architecture & Level Breakdown

The simulation is structured around a sequential 5-day training program, tracking accumulated player points (Puntos) and enforcing strict resource management (energy, time, and precision).

  • Day 1: Spacecraft Stabilization, Rations & Power Grid
    • Stabilization: Teaches spacecraft structural engineering principles by choosing a 3-legged equilateral triangular base over a square to handle irregular Martian rock surfaces.
    • Food Supply: Focuses on long-duration space food management, combining weekly nutrient menu planning with vacuum-sealed aluminum storage compartments.
    • Power Generation: Implements a randomized button-sequence puzzle (A, B, C, D, E) where players manually reconnect backup power systems, featuring dynamic position hints and point deductions for incorrect attempts.
    • Challenges players to chart precise movement paths (Right, Left, Straight) across major Martian landmarks: Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, Jezero Crater (Perseverance landing site), and Gale Crater.
    • Simulates a tactical rover expedition balancing speed, hill scaling, dune navigation, sandstorm shelter choices, and return paths, calculating dynamic metrics for Energy, Rover Integrity, and Time.
    • Tests scientific identification skills against a comprehensive guide of 10 Martian soil types and rock formations (such as Basaltic Regolith, Hematite Blueberries, Gypsum Crystals, Perchlorate Soil, and Duricrust), utilizing randomized sample rounds and multi-tier scoring.
    • Antena Alignment & Messaging: Manages radio wave trajectories across Earth-Mars distances (55M–400M km) while dealing with signal degradation from sandstorms.
    • Data Decoding: Decodes an encrypted numeric sequence (7, 18, 1, 14, 4...) into text pointing to the sample landing site (Grand Cay, The Bahamas).
    • Orbital Mechanics & Launch: Manages launch energy thresholds and executes a final compressed air trajectory correction maneuver past the Moon's orbit to ensure safe arrival.

3. Scientific Disclosure & NASA Data Integration

The project relies strictly on validated aerospace and planetary science data:

  • Spacecraft & Lander Design: Structural stability guidelines adapted from NASA planetary landers.
  • Martian Geology & Topography: Real-world cartography of volcanoes, canyons, and active rover exploration sites (Perseverance and Curiosity footprints).
  • Deep Space Network (DSN): Real-world astrodynamics, signal propagation delays, and antenna positioning parameters.

4. Migration to HTML/Web Interface

While the core logic and algorithmic structures were prototyped and validated in Python scripts (Juegocompleto.py through Juegocompletto_4.py), the project was translated into HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the final deployment.

  • UI/UX Enhancement: Replaced console text inputs (input()) and terminal color codes (\033[...]) with responsive web forms, buttons, and dynamic display containers.
  • Accessibility: Allowed seamless browser-based execution during the live presentation without requiring a local Python interpreter environment.
